title.zh: 卷二百一十 表第一 宰輔一
title.raw: 卷二百一十 表第一 宰輔一 Volume 210 Tables 1: Chancellors 1

sentences.zh: 宋宰輔年表，前九朝始建隆庚申，終靖康丙午，凡一百六十七年，居相位者七十二人，位執政者二百三十八人。

translations.literal: Song chancellors annual table: for the first nine reigns, beginning at Jianlong gengshen, ending at Jingkang bingwu, altogether one hundred sixty-seven years; those who held the chancellorship, seventy-two persons; those who held executive posts, two hundred thirty-eight persons.
translations.idiomatic: This table of Song chancellors covers the first nine reigns from Jianlong in the year gengshen of 960 through Jingkang in the year bingwu of 1126—167 years in all—in which seventy-two men held the chief ministership and 238 served as executive councillors.

sentences.zh: 後七朝始建炎丁未，終德祐丙子，凡一百四十九年，居相位者六十一人，位執政者二百四十四人。

translations.literal: The latter seven reigns, beginning at Jianyan dingwei, ending at Deyou bingzi, altogether one hundred forty-nine years; those who held the chancellorship, sixty-one persons; those who held executive posts, two hundred forty-four persons.
translations.idiomatic: The last seven reigns run from Jianyan in the year dingwei of 1127 to Deyou in the year bingzi of 1276—149 years—with sixty-one chancellors and 244 executive councillors.

sentences.zh: 敘古曰：古之史法主於編年，至司馬遷作《史記》始易以新意，然國家世祚，人事歲月，散于紀、傳、世家，先後始終，遽難考見，此表之不可無，而編年不容於盡變也。

translations.literal: Narrating antiquity says: ancient historiographical method chiefly relied on annals; when Sima Qian composed the 《Records of the Grand Historian》 he first changed it with a new conception, yet national dynastic fortunes and human affairs through the months and years, scattered in annals, biographies, and hereditary houses, their sequence, beginning, and end—suddenly difficult to examine and see—this is why tables cannot be dispensed with, while annals cannot permit being wholly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: The preface to antiquity observes that early historiography was chiefly annalistic until Sima Qian reshaped the craft in his 《Records》. Even so, a dynasty's span and the chronology of men's careers lie scattered across annals, biographies, and house histories, so that sequence and term are hard to trace at a glance—hence tables are indispensable, and the annal form cannot be abandoned entirely.

sentences.zh: 厥後班固《漢史》乃曰《百官公卿表》，先敘官名、職秩、印授等，然後書年以表其姓名。

translations.literal: Thereafter Ban Gu's 《History of Han》 was titled the 《Table of the Hundred Offices and Dukes and Ministers》; first narrating office names, ranks and duties, seal bestowals and the like, then writing years to tabulate their personal names.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Ban Gu's 《History of Han》 included the 《Table of Officials and Ministers》, which first sets out titles, ranks, and seals of appointment and then lists names year by year.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修《唐史》又專以宰相名篇，意必有所在矣。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu's 《History of Tang》 again devoted a section specifically to chancellors by name; the intent surely had its place.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu's 《History of Tang》 likewise devotes a separate section to chancellors—a choice that surely answered to some need.

sentences.zh: 宋自太祖至欽宗，舊史雖以《三朝》、《兩朝》、《四朝》各自為編，而年表未有成書。

translations.literal: Song from Taizu to Qinzong: although the old histories took the 《Three Reigns》, 《Two Reigns》, and 《Four Reigns》 each as separate compilations, an annual table had not yet become a completed book.
translations.idiomatic: From Taizu through Qinzong the older histories were compiled as separate works for the Three, Two, and 《Four Reigns》, but no complete annual table of ministers was ever produced.

sentences.zh: 神宗時常命陳繹檢閱二府除罷官職事，因為《拜罷錄》。

translations.literal: During Shenzong's time he often ordered Chen Yi to examine the Two Offices' appointments and dismissals and official matters, and on that basis composed the 《Record of Appointments and Dismissals》.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shenzong, Chen Yi was repeatedly ordered to review appointments and removals in the Two Departments and compiled the 《Record of Appointments and Dismissals》.

sentences.zh: 元豐間，司馬光嘗敘宋興以來百官公卿沿革除拜，作年表上之史館。

translations.literal: During the Yuanfeng era, Sima Guang once narrated from Song's rise onward the hundred offices and dukes and ministers' evolution, removals and appointments, composed an annual table and presented it to the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanfeng period Sima Guang drafted an annual table tracing appointments and changes among Song officials from the founding of the dynasty and submitted it to the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 自時而後，曾鞏、譚世勣、蔡幼學、李燾諸人皆嘗續為之。

translations.literal: From that time onward, Zeng Gong, Tan Shiji, Cai Youxue, Li Tao, and others all once continued it.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Zeng Gong, Tan Shiji, Cai Youxue, Li Tao, and others each attempted continuations.

sentences.zh: 然表文簡嚴，世罕知好，故多淪落無傳。

translations.literal: Yet table texts are concise and severe; the age rarely knows to esteem them, so many sank into oblivion without transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Such tables are terse and austere, however, and few readers valued them, so most of these works were lost.

sentences.zh: 今纂修《宋史》，故一以實錄為據，旁搜博采紀、傳以為是表。

translations.literal: Now compiling and revising the 《History of Song》, therefore taking the Veritable Records alone as basis, searching widely and gathering broadly from annals and biographies to make this table.
translations.idiomatic: In compiling the present 《History of Song》 we rely chiefly on the Veritable Records, supplementing them with material drawn from annals and biographies to form this table.

sentences.zh: 其間所書宰輔官、職、勳、爵、館、殿、職、名，間有不同者，官制沿革有時而異也。

translations.literal: Among them what is written of chancellors' offices, duties, orders of merit, enfeoffments, institutes, halls, posts, and names—at times there are differences—because the bureaucratic system's evolution and removals differ according to the times.
translations.idiomatic: Where titles, offices, honors, ranks, institute posts, and hall appointments recorded for chancellors differ from entry to entry, that reflects changes in the bureaucracy over time.

sentences.zh: 然中書位次既止於參知政事，而樞府職序自同知、副使而下雖簽書、同簽書亦與焉者，皆執政也，故不得而略焉。

translations.literal: Yet because the Secretariat's ranking stopped at Vice Grand Councillor, while the Bureau of Military Affairs' sequence from Associate Director and Deputy Commissioner downward—even Signing Secretary and Associate Signing Secretary when included—are all executive ministers, therefore they cannot be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Although the highest Secretariat rank entered here is Vice Grand Councillor, every post in the Bureau of Military Affairs from Associate Director and Deputy Commissioner down—including Signing Secretary and Associate Signing Secretary when held concurrently—counts as an executive minister and is therefore included.

sentences.zh: 夫大臣之用舍，關於世道之隆汙，千載而下，將使覽者即表之年觀紀及傳之事，此登載之不容於不謹也。

translations.literal: Great ministers' employment and dismissal bear upon the age's rise and corruption; a thousand years hence, they will enable viewers by the table's years to observe annals' and biographies' affairs—this recording cannot permit inattention.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment and removal of great ministers bears on whether an age flourishes or declines; centuries hence readers should be able to read this table's chronology against the annals and biographies, so the record must be compiled with care.

sentences.zh: 表之所書，雖無褒貶是非於其間，然歲月昭於上，姓名著於下，則不惟其人之賢佞邪正可指而議，而當時任用之專否，政治之得失，皆可得而見矣。

translations.literal: What the table writes, although without praise and blame and right and wrong within it, yet with months and years displayed above and personal names set forth below, then not only can each person's worth, flattery, wickedness, and uprightness be pointed to and discussed, but the age's employment as exclusive or not, and government's gains and losses—all can be obtained and seen.
translations.idiomatic: The table offers no explicit moral verdict, yet with dates above and names below one may judge each man's character and also discern whether appointments were concentrated or shared and where governance succeeded or failed.

sentences.zh: 後之覽者，其必有所勸也夫，其亦有所戒也夫！

translations.literal: Later viewers surely will have something to be encouraged by! Surely also something to be warned by!
translations.idiomatic: Readers to come will surely find in it both encouragement and warning!

translations.literal: Second month, day jihai: Wu Tingzuo, from Commissioner of Military Affairs, added Grand Councilor. Fifth month, day jiwei: the emperor personally campaigned against Li Yun; Wu Tingzuo remained as Eastern Capital garrison commander. Eighth month, day wuzi: Zhao Pu, from Right Remonstrance Grand Master, Direct Academician of Military Affairs, and Vice Minister of War, added Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs. Eleventh month, day dinghai: the emperor personally campaigned against Li Chongjin; Wu Tingzuo Eastern Capital garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai of the second month Wu Tingzuo was promoted from Military Affairs Commissioner to Grand Councilor. On jiwei of the fifth month the emperor campaigned in person against Li Yun, leaving Wu Tingzuo as garrison commander of the Eastern Capital. On wuzi of the eighth month Zhao Pu rose from Right Remonstrance Counselor, privy council academician, and Vice Minister of War to Deputy Military Affairs Commissioner. On dinghai of the eleventh month the emperor campaigned against Li Chongjin; Wu Tingzuo again held the Eastern Capital command.

Seventh month, day gengchen: Li Fang, from Wenhua Hall academician and Minister of Works retaining his original office, was made Vice Grand Councillor. Eleventh month, day renshen: Li Mu, from Hanlin Academician and prefect of Kaifeng; Lü Mengzheng, from Hanlin Academician and Outer Section Member of the Capital Office; Li Zhi, from Hanlin Academician, Capital Office Section Chief, and drafter of edicts—all were made Vice Grand Councillors. Zhang Qixian and Wang Han, from direct academicians of the Bureau of Military Affairs, were both transferred to Right Remonstrance Grandee and Associate Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Twelfth month: Li Mu entered mourning for his mother and was recalled from mourning.

On jihai of the sixth month Wang Xian was promoted from Deputy Military Affairs Commissioner to Inspector-General Grand Guardian and Military Affairs Commissioner. On gengchen of the seventh month Li Fang, retaining his Wenhua Hall academician and Works ministership, was appointed Vice Grand Councillor. On renshen of the eleventh month Li Mu, Lü Mengzheng, and Li Zhi were all made Vice Grand Councillors from their respective Hanlin and Capital Office posts; Zhang Qixian and Wang Han moved from Military Affairs direct academicians to Right Remonstrance Grandee and Associate Signing Secretary. In the twelfth month Li Mu entered mourning for his mother and was recalled to duty.
